topic: Individuals, Firms, Markets and Market Failure
subject: economics

moments.title: The Market for Lemons
moments.body: Akerlof shows that asymmetric information about quality can cause markets to unravel, using used cars as the example.
moments.takeaway: Information asymmetries are a major source of market failure.

moments.title: Job Market Signaling
moments.body: Spence shows education can serve as a costly signal in labour markets even when it does not raise productivity.
moments.takeaway: Signalling can sustain markets in the presence of asymmetry.

moments.title: Nobel Prize
moments.body: The Nobel Prize is awarded for the analysis of markets with asymmetric information.
moments.takeaway: Information economics is recognised as foundational.

now.title: Information asymmetries online
now.body: Online reviews, ratings and algorithmic intermediation are analysed through Akerlof's framework.
now.open_questions: Do platform reputation systems solve or merely shift asymmetric-information problems?

reflection: Akerlof's paper was famously rejected by multiple journals before publication.
